Case at a Glance

The problem

First-time investors under 30 find mutual fund investing intimidating. On Groww, some sign up but never make a first investment.

2 of 9 interviewees created an account and never invested.
What we heard

Knowing what to pick is the biggest hurdle: 7 of 9 named too many choices or lack of knowledge.

All 3 who had never invested asked for step-by-step gamified guides.
What we propose

Learn & Earn: bite-sized lessons, quizzes and quests that reward learning, never investing.

Supported by guided account setup and a virtual-coin simulator (to be tested).
How we measure it

North Star: 90-day SIP retention, the share of new users with an active SIP 90 days after their first mutual fund investment.

Guardrails: SIP cancellations, early redemptions, complaints.

OVERVIEW

About: Groww is a financial services platform based in India that primarily focuses on investment and wealth management. It was founded in 2016 and offers a user-friendly interface for individuals to invest in various financial instruments.

Mission: To democratize access to financial services for millions of Indians by making investing simple, transparent, and accessible for everyone.

Vision: To empower every individual in India with the knowledge, tools, and confidence to make informed financial decisions-becoming the trusted financial partner for millions of Indians.

Breaking down the 5 Whys

Why 1

Why do first-time users under 30 find mutual fund investing intimidating on Groww?

First-time users find investing intimidating because they lack fundamental knowledge about mutual funds and investing principles. Young investors often struggle with selecting the right fund from numerous options, understanding fund factsheets, and interpreting performance metrics

Why 2

Why do young users lack knowledge and confidence about mutual fund investing?

Financial education is not consistently included in India's standard educational curriculum, creating a knowledge gap among young adults. Young professionals entering the workforce have limited exposure to financial markets and may encounter overwhelming and contradictory information online

Data point: only 27% of Indian adults are financially literate (NCFE survey, 2019)
Why 3

Why is this knowledge gap more pronounced among users under 30?

Users under 30 have less investing experience and typically more limited disposable income, making them more risk-averse with their early earnings. Unlike previous generations, today's young investors face a paradox of choice with thousands of investment options

Why 4

Why isn't the current onboarding process effectively addressing these knowledge gaps?

The current onboarding process likely assumes baseline financial knowledge that many first-time investors don't possess. The process may lack sufficient positive reinforcement for taking initial steps, failing to counteract the anxiety of financial decision-making.

Why 5 · Root cause

The first-run experience assumes knowledge users don’t have and gives no reward for small first steps.

Our bet

Gamification

Teach in small steps and reward each step, so confidence builds before the first investment.

Source: NCFE National Financial Literacy and Inclusion Survey 2019 (27% figure). Other answers are team hypotheses from desk research.

Background

  • A young professional with a stable job in software, recently started exploring mutual fund investments, motivated by long-term wealth creation.
  • Limited prior knowledge; initial investments influenced by trusted colleague’s advice.
  • Slightly high risk appetite but cautious due to lack of experience.
  • Uses digital tools like Splitwise and GPay for expense tracking; prefers digital-first financial management.

Goals

  • To understand mutual funds in simple terms and reduce fear of losing money.
  • To confidently make the first mutual fund investment and build a habit of regular investing.

Pains

  • Feeling overwhelmed by complex terms and too many fund options.
  • Fear of losing hard-earned money, especially when investments fluctuate.
  • Lack of confidence to invest without expert guidance.

Needs

  • Mock investing or interactive tools to practice with virtual money.
  • Easy-to-understand onboarding that explains mutual funds step-by-step.
  • Clear and honest info about risks and benefits.

Solution - Learn & Earn Feature

What is this feature?

An interactive module with bite-sized videos, quizzes, personalized tips, and rewards. Users learn investment basics, test their knowledge, and earn XP points to unlock premium tools.

How will this work?

Users learn through bite-sized lessons on key investment topics, take quizzes to reinforce learning, and receive a personalized learning path and fund-category explainers based on their progress. Daily and weekly quests keep engagement high, while users earn XP points that can be redeemed for learning rewards like expert webinars or advanced tools. Rewards are earned for learning, never for investing. Progress is tracked through badges, leaderboards, and milestones, making the journey fun, rewarding, and confidence-boosting for first-time investors.

v1 scope: bite-sized lessons, quizzes, XP and daily quests. Leaderboards come later, opt-in and based on learning only.

Groww today: free learning content already exists (blogs, videos, in-app explainers). What Learn & Earn adds: a structured path with quizzes, quests and rewards that turns that content into a first investment.

Account Setup with Guided Learning

What is this feature?

A simplified onboarding flow with an optional beginner-friendly guide to help users set up a Demat account with confidence.

How will this work?

New users see a pop-up prompt to open a Demat account, with an option to toggle on a "Beginner's Guide." If selected, they’re taken to a short explainer video that simplifies the process, followed by a clear CTA button to proceed. Users who prefer to skip the guide can directly start the account setup. Both paths lead to a streamlined and unified Demat account creation experience.

What Problem it solves?

  • Reduces confusion and drop-offs during onboarding
  • Supports first-time users with easy guidance
  • Increases sign-ups and completion rates
  • Builds user trust and confidence from the start

Why this matters

  • Interviews: 3 of 9 found onboarding complex, 2 created an account but never invested, 2 uninstalled the app
  • A demat account is optional for mutual funds, so for MF-first users the guide covers KYC and account setup
  • Design guardrail: the explainer is skippable and under 60 seconds, so the guide does not lengthen onboarding

Source: Groww blog, “Why you don’t need a demat account to invest in mutual funds”.

Virtual Coin Investment Feature

Hypothesis to test

What is this feature?

A risk-free way for users to try investing before their first real investment, using virtual coins on historical fund data, so they see how long-term investing behaves before using real money.

How will this work?

New users get virtual coins to invest in real mutual funds using historical NAVs, for example seeing what ₹500 a month would have grown to over 5 years. They get learning tips along the way, and can move to real investing when ready.

What Problem it solves?

  • Builds confidence before the first investment
  • Teaches long-term thinking, not short-term swings
  • Improves financial literacy
  • Increases engagement and conversion

Evidence so far

  • One interviewee asked for a “mock platform to get used to idea of trading or investing in stocks”
  • Historical data keeps it within SEBI’s limits on sharing live market prices

Source: SEBI norms on sharing real-time price data (2024; education lag revised to 30 days in 2026).

What We’d Validate Next

Our research is directional: 9 structured interviews in a 48-hour sprint. Before building, we would test these four things.

Talk to more first-time investors

Run 20 more interviews with people who have never invested in mutual funds.

Today: only 3 of our 9 interviewees had never invested.

Find the real drop-off point

Use Groww’s funnel data from sign-up to KYC to first mutual fund investment.

Today: 2 of 9 created an account but never invested.

Clear compliance early

Review recommendation cards, rewards and the simulator against SEBI rules on advice, inducements and market price data.

Design principle: reward learning, never investing.

Measure what lasts

A/B test with a holdout group and track 90-day SIP retention, not only 7-day conversion.

Guardrails: SIP cancellations and early redemptions.
